title: AP Biology Independent Foundation Pilot
description: An independently authored 500-question AP Biology foundation pilot spanning all eight current units. It tests the blueprint crosswalk, science-practice metadata, structured native chapter lessons, cumulative scenario reasoning, molecular evidence, energy-flow accounting, and internal QA before any official or release-ready expansion.
disclaimer: Independent, unofficial AP Biology preparation material for internal foundation-pilot development only. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or authored by College Board. This pilot does not provide official scores, score predictions, college-credit predictions, laboratory competency, or a substitute for supervised laboratory work.
contentReview: Five hundred original source-aligned draft multiple-choice items: sixty to sixty-five per current AP Biology unit, with all six science practices represented, unit and topic remediation routes, cumulative multi-unit scenarios, evidence evaluation, molecular evidence, quantitative genetics, energy-flow accounting, and eight structured native lessons. Independent AP Biology subject-expert, laboratory, rights, accessibility, production, field-testing, and psychometric review remain pending.

items.prompt: A parent with genotype I to the A I to the B has a child with a parent of genotype I to the A i. What is the probability that their child has type B blood?

items.rationale: The first parent produces I to the A or I to the B gametes and the second produces I to the A or i gametes; only I to the B i gives type B, so the probability is one-fourth.

items.prompt: A population is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium and has a recessive phenotype frequency of 0.04. What fraction of the population is expected to be heterozygous?

bigIdeas.label: Evolution

bigIdeas.label: Energetics
